item.title: Red State
item.description: Violence repeats. Power repeats. Disbelief repeats. This poem unearths the weight of history, protest, and the quiet resilience buried beneath it all.

item.title: I don’t really go for Marvel movies but
item.description: There’s that one scene. Vision and Wanda on a cobbled Edinburgh street. His voice trembling, her touch reassuring. That aching, quiet desperation of asking someone to love you, let you love them. It’s raw. It’s human. It’s everything.

item.title: His girlfriend dumped him, and he started cutting again.
item.description: "Starling phalanx westward on the grass, jabbing the earth, at one moment uncertain what they see is real..." A powerful, haunting poem where the restless flight of starlings becomes a metaphor for grief, longing, and resilience. One man

item.title: Accessible? To Whom?
item.description: The essay critiques the misconception that online poetry events are more accessible and community-driven than in-person gatherings. While virtual platforms offer convenience and global reach, they fall short of providing the authentic connection, safety, and shared humanity that live events foster.

item.title: No Running In The Graveyard
item.description: A hauntingly beautiful poem about children’s games played among tombstones, where laughter and broken glass meet quiet reverence. The dead are remembered, their names spoken, and their presence honored in the only way the children know how.

item.title: Our Struggle Series: What Is and Isn
item.description: What separates real politics from performance? In the latest Our Struggle, we dismantle symbolic leftist politics.

item.title: Vampire Girl: Chapters 28-32
item.description: As Mayra’s stage power rises, the Trampire unveils a radical plan to buy back the Gadsden Purchase and create a vampires-only republic. Fame, ideology, and supernatural ambition collide in the sharp, satirical Vampire Girl.

item.title: Our Struggle Series: The Politics That Isn
item.description: This essay critiques individualist anarchism and centrism as ideologies of political avoidance. Using Stirner’s egoism as a case study, it argues that reducing morality to private will severs politics from shared material reality. Centrism, likewise, preserves hierarchy by aestheticizing balance. As part of Our Struggle, the essay insists that real politics requires confrontation with power, collective consequence, and material conditions.

item.title: The Dead Writers Club
item.description: "The Dead Writers Club" is a comic afterlife symposium where dead writers bicker, snack, misquote one another, fight over fire-making duties, and stage an annual Fireside Story Competition. A satirical literary séance full of ego, ritual, anachronism, and wordplay.

item.title: Our Struggle Series: False Flags: When Non-Leftist Agendas Disguise Themselves as Leftist Struggle
item.description: "False Flags" is a critique of performative politics and ideological drift within the modern left. Drawing on moral realism (Nagel), and perennial ethical traditions, it argues that emancipation requires discipline, coherence, and internal accountability.
